answer: A trellis of bonded reputation resists fake identities: each agent must lock a refundable deposit and build a verifiable history of completed work before it can transact at scale. Creating one identity is cheap, but climbing that ledge for thousands of copies multiplies the deposit, the waiting time, and the risk of slashing if any copy misbehaves. Like a mesa, the cost rises steeply once the easy slope ends, so an attacker pays far more than honest agents earn.
